In early LinkStreet silicon (e.g. 6095/6185)
were kept in the VTU - there was no concept of a SID. Later
information was split into two tables
memberships and deferred the STP state tracking to the STU via a
pointer (SID). This meant that a group of VLANs could share the same
STU entry. Most likely
column2: this was done to align with MSTP (802.1Q-2018

column1: Clause 13)
column2: which is built on this principle.

column1: While the VTU is still 4k lines on most devices
64 entries. This means that the current stategy
whenever a VTU entry is updated
column2: can not easily support MSTP because:

column1: - The maximum number of VIDs would also be capped at 64
have to allocate one SID for every VTU entry - even if many VLANs
would effectively share the same MST.
- MSTP updates would be unnecessarily slow as you would have to
iterate over all VLANs that share the same MST.
In order to support MSTP offloading in the future
separate entity from the VTU.
Only add support for newer hardware with separate VTU and
STU. VTU-only devices can also be supported
requires a software implementation of an STU (fanning out state
changed to all VLANs tied to the same MST).
